lines.text: Which drain cleaner actually eats a hair clog?
ai: a bathroom sink drain clogged with a clump of hair under dramatic light

lines.text: He drops hair and soap and grease and even tape into every product for twelve hours.
ai: clear glass jars with hair and grease and soap inside

lines.text: And the clear winner on hair is plain lye.
ai: a jar of white lye crystals on a dark shelf

lines.text: Because hair is made of protein and lye chops those protein chains apart until the clog dissolves.
ai: macro of a single human hair dissolving in liquid
glowing protein chains snapping apart macro
hair strands dissolving into bubbles in a glass

lines.text: Drano and Liquid Plumber tie with it because they're mostly lye too with some bleach.
ai: three drain cleaner bottles in a row on a bathroom floor

lines.text: The enzyme sticks just turn everything blue because bacteria work slowly over days.
ai: bright blue liquid swirling in a drain
tiny bacteria under a microscope glowing

lines.text: And the acids eat a carrot but also strip the plating off a steel pipe.
ai: a carrot dissolving in a glass of bubbling acid

lines.text: So acid works on food clogs but it attacks metal which is why it's only safe for plastic pipes.
ai: acid eating the shiny plating off a steel pipe macro
a clean white plastic pipe under a sink

lines.text: Nothing touched the paper towel or tape so for solid stuff a drain snake beats every bottle here.
ai: a metal drain snake coiled on a bathroom floor

lines.text: And never mix them because bleach plus acid makes toxic chlorine gas.
ai: a toxic green cloud of gas rising from a sink
two cleaning bottles with a red warning glow

lines.text: So what's really clogging your drain?
ai: a bathroom sink drain clogged with a clump of hair under dramatic light
